sections.headline: Six players tied at -6 lead Round 1 at Colonial, with Gerard's +4.78 total SG and hot putter setting the pace.
sections.leaders: Andrew Putnam, J.J. Spaun, Lee Hodges, Matt McCarty, Ryan Gerard, and Tom Kim all shot 64s to share the lead at -6. Gerard leads the SG leaderboard with +4.78 total, gaining +4.24 strokes with the putter despite losing -1.20 off-the-tee. Spaun matches Gerard's total SG at +4.78 with a more balanced attack: +1.51 approach, +1.19 off-the-tee, +1.77 putting.

on_fire.name: Ryan Gerard
on_fire.blurb: Gerard's +4.24 putting SG is the round's most dominant single category despite ranking T1 in total SG alongside 5 others. He's gaining strokes everywhere except off-the-tee (-1.20), relying on approach play (+2.91) to set up scoring opportunities.

on_fire.name: Ricky Castillo
on_fire.blurb: Castillo sits T7 at -5 with the sharpest approach game on the leaderboard: +4.15 SG approach. His off-the-tee and putting are neutral (+0.16 and -0.17), but that approach dominance is keeping him within 1 stroke of the lead.

on_fire.name: Lee Hodges
on_fire.blurb: Hodges shares the lead at -6 with the second-best putting day: +3.63 strokes gained on the greens. His approach (+1.40) is solid, and he's managing the tee shot (-0.65) well enough to stay tied at the top.

to_watch.name: Brian Harman
to_watch.blurb: Harman at T7 (-5) is just 1 back with +2.47 approach SG and +0.54 off-the-tee gain. His putter is quiet (+0.50), suggesting room for scoring acceleration if it gets hot over the next 3 rounds.

to_watch.name: Keegan Bradley
to_watch.blurb: Bradley sits T7 at -5 with +1.38 off-the-tee SG and +2.46 putting—balanced scoring that tracks well at Colonial. He's only 1 stroke back with clean long-game numbers.

to_watch.name: Billy Horschel
to_watch.blurb: Horschel at T7 (-5) has the experience and recent form to stay in contention. His +3.78 total SG ties the T7 pack, and Colonial's course history often rewards seasoned players through 4 rounds.

sections.your_picks: Gerard at T1 (-6) and Tom Kim at T1 (-6) are in ideal spot—both tied for the lead with 2 and 1 uses left, respectively. Gerard's hot putter and Kim's balanced +4.78 SG suggest both can advance, though Gerard's season SG of +0.28 and recent 70.9 scoring average offer more trajectory confidence than Kim's -0.13 season SG. Your T19 cluster (Hisatsune -4, Henley -4, Thorbjornsen -4, Matsuyama -4) are 2 back but need a bounce from recent form: Henley's 69.6 scoring average stands out, and Thorbjornsen's +0.47 season SG is the group's strongest foundation.
sections.round_story: Scoring at Colonial is hot—6 players already at -6 after 18 holes, with 12 more at -5 or better. The putter is the differentiator: Gerard and Hodges led with +4.24 and +3.63 putting SG, while even mid-pack players like Bradley and Kim are gaining +2.46 and +3.24 on the greens. Off-the-tee play is secondary; approach shots are driving separation, with Ricky Castillo's +4.15 approach gain setting the standard for greens-hitting dominance.
